My read of the mandate

Not a maintenance job. A simplification job.

The posting is clear: rethink how the platform is used, retire technical debt, speed up delivery for marketing operations, and bring agents into how the team builds and runs Marketing Cloud. I read that as three connected outcomes.

Simplify

Fewer patterns, clearer standards

Rationalize data extension design and integration patterns into a small set of governed standards, so every new CDP, CRM, or warehouse feed follows a known path instead of a one-off build.

Speed

Shorter path from brief to send

Measure campaign build cycle time and delivery predictability, then remove the steps that add risk without adding value. Reusable journey, content, and data templates do most of the work.

Agentic delivery

Agents on the repetitive work

Put agents on scaffolding, QA, testing, and monitoring through native tooling or API and MCP connections, inside the bank's model-risk and change controls, so technologists spend their time on architecture.

Context: RBC is one of Salesforce's most public financial-services partners. RBC Wealth Management's published Salesforce story describes 26 disconnected systems consolidated and a first Agentforce agent launched in six weeks. Consolidation and agentic delivery have already worked inside this organization.

First 180 days

Listen, simplify, then accelerate

A plan I would pressure-test in the first conversations, not impose. The order matters: standards and baselines come before agents.

Days 0–30
Listen and map
  • Meet marketing operations, data and CDP, and technology partners; learn what slows them down today.
  • Inventory business units, data extensions, automations, journeys, integrations, and send volumes by channel.
  • Baseline speed to market, delivery predictability, and stakeholder satisfaction.
  • Meet every member of the team one to one; understand skills, ambitions, and pain points.
Days 30–90
Simplify
  • Publish data extension and integration standards, with governance for consent, privacy, and security.
  • Pick the three pieces of technical debt with the biggest drag and retire them.
  • Stand up delivery health metrics: cycle time, predictability, and rework.
  • Land one visible quick win on a high-volume campaign build path.
Days 90–180
Accelerate
  • Pilot agents on two repeatable workflows, such as journey and data extension scaffolding and pre-send QA.
  • Run pilots under model-risk, audit, and change-management controls from day one.
  • Publish a platform roadmap tied to measured outcomes and budget trade-offs.
  • Build a team skills plan so Marketing Cloud and agentic expertise deepens across the practice.

How I see the practice

RBC's Marketing Cloud practice, layer by layer

Salesforce publishes a four-layer reference architecture for the agentic enterprise. Mapping this practice onto it shows where simplification and agents pay off first.

System of Engagement · the channelsEmail, mobile push, and SMS reaching millions of clients every day, plus the internal workspace where marketers and technologists collaborate.
System of Agency · agentic deliveryAgents that scaffold journeys and data extensions, run pre-send QA and regression tests, and watch integrations, through native tooling or API and MCP connections.
System of Work · journeys and automationsJourney Builder, Automation Studio, and content standards that marketing operations relies on, governed as reusable patterns.
System of Context · data foundationCDP, CRM, and data warehouse feeds landing in well-designed data extensions, with identity and consent resolved upstream.
TRUST · CONSENT · AUDIT
Model substrate: whichever foundation models the bank approves sit beneath the stack. Where models run and how they are validated is a governance decision, not a feature decision.

Layer names are Salesforce's published reference architecture. My contribution is the operating model: which standards, owners, and controls sit at each layer.
